question: Tuzuk-i-Baburi/Baburnama was originally written in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chagatai**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**, also known as **Baburnama**, was originally written in **Chagatai**.
 
• **Chagatai** was the native language of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire.
 
• It is an autobiography of Babur, providing a detailed account of his life, conquests, and the socio-political environment of his time.
 
• The work is regarded as one of the most important historical documents of the Mughal era and offers invaluable insights into the history and culture of Central Asia and India during Babur's reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur** was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side, which influenced his cultural and linguistic heritage.
 
• The **Baburnama** was later translated into Persian during the reign of Babur's grandson, Akbar, making it accessible to a wider audience in the Mughal Empire.
 
• The autobiography not only covers military campaigns but also provides descriptions of the flora, fauna, and geography of the regions Babur conquered.
 
• Babur's vivid and candid writing style in the **Baburnama** has been praised by historians and scholars for its authenticity and richness of detail.
